newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN SHARES DRIFT LOWER, UNRATTLED BY KOKH.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN SHARES DRIFT LOWER, UNRATTLED BY KOKH.

text.p: Russian shares eased slightly on Wednesday, with the resignation of Russian privatisation chief Alfred Kokh having little effect after a mostly directionless session dominated by Russian speculators, traders said.
They said a positive report on U.S. industrial prices had boosted shares, but most leading stocks had edged down to slightly below Tuesday's closing prices by the end of the day.
The Russian Trading System 21-share index eased less than one percent to 552.62 from 557.99 on Tuesday while total market turnover was a mediocre $63.5 million.
United City Bank head of equity trading Samit Yakovlev did not see Kokh's resignation, announced shortly before the market closed, shaking the market significantly.
"I cannot say that Kokh's resignation is a catastrophe for the market," Yakovlev said.
But he said a better-than-expected U.S. producer price index, which slipped 0.1 percent in July, had jolted prices upwards.

"The American data were very positive and the market rose sharply immediately afterward," said Yakovlev, seeing another rise on Thursday. "I think some speculative Western clients will again start to be interested in Russian stock."
LUKoil firmed to $27.55 from $27.36, but national power company UES ticked down to $0.4355 from $0.4404. Regional utility Mosenergo eased to $1.690 from $1.697.
One Western trader said new money was flowing into liquid stocks from smaller investors, while old clients were keeping their positions.

"They are waiting for a one hundred percent profit in less liquid shares," the trader said. "It's silly to talk about that growth in liquid shares, of course, but they are also hoping for a small rise there."

International long-distance provider Rostelekom RTKM.RTS sagged to $4.76 from $4.85, and Yakovlev said news that the Russian government was investigating last month's sale of a quarter of holding company Svyazinvest did not help prices.
"There seems to be a question mark hanging over the fate of the Svyazinvest auction, and that is not the best news for Rostelekom," he said.
